title: AP_Motors: Dualheli- fix bug for scaling second swashplate
body:
This PR is being submitted to fix an issue found with the second swashplate not being scaled to the H_COL2_MIN and H_COL2_MAX parameters.  Discuss Forum user Tudole posted the issue [here](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/possible-bug-in-dual-rotor/36368)

This issue was a result of the code change associated with the PR #8739.  the servo position calculations for each swashplate are now broken out as they were prior to PR#8739 so as to account for the different scaling between the two swashplates.

In addition I moved the if statement that applies the H_LAND_COL_MIN  parameter to the collective so that it is applied to both of the swashplates.

I conducted a functional check in the SITL to ensure there were no issues with the change.  I verified that the limits of each swashplate were dictated by the corresponding parameters.  IMO, no flight test is required.

title: Fixes EKF2 terrain estimator use of optical flow data
body: The single state estimator used by EKF2 to estimate height was designed to able to use both range finder and optical flow data to estimate the offset of terrain under the vehicle. The observation equations for use of optical flow data do not match the source derivation and appear to have been carried cross from an earlier derivation that used the length of the motion compensated optical flow vector. The fusion of a vector length instead of separate X and Y components resulted in rectification of noise at small ground speed / height ratio values, eg: It is also unable to fuse data where the noise is large enough to causes the reading to change sign. There was a simple vector length check that required the length to be > 0.01 rad/sec, but this did not work effectively. The original filter and modified version was tested using the following PMW3901 flow sensor https://www.tindie.com/products/onehorse/pmw3901-optical-flow-sensor/ connected via SPI interface. The scale default scale factor had to be increased 55% by setting both the FLOW_FXSCALER and FLOW_FYSCALER parameters to 550 to get the gyro and flow data to match, eg: Airborne testing at higher speed/height ratios also confirmed the revised calibration, eg: The observation equations were then updated to be consistent with https://github.com/PX4/ecl/tree/master/EKF/matlab/scripts/Terrain%20Estimatowith addition of a parameter to control if optical flow data is used by the navigation and/or the terrain estimator. Preliminary flight testing shows much improved performance, however further tuning with flight over more undulating terrain is still required. Complete flight: Landing:

title: AC_Avoidance: fix BendyRuler when outside polygon fence
body:
This PR resolves this issue: https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/11543 in which the vehicle would actively stay outside the polygon fence if for some reason it managed to get outside of it.

This fix modifies the calculation of the margin from the polygon fence to be the **negative** of the closest point (from the fence) on the line being probed.  Below is an image which helps to show why this is the correct way to calculate the margin.
![bendy-ruler-margin-calc-pic](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/59320202-6f6a4100-8d08-11e9-98e5-b782a66b15d9.png)

Here are a few screen shots of the vehicle's behaviour when BendyRuler is activated outside the fence.  
![bendy-ruler-fix](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/59320224-8872f200-8d08-11e9-95ff-337a03289009.png)
- The left image shows the vehicle outside the fence.
- The middle image shows the vehicle's final destination is waypoint 1 (see the red line) but it first moves in the direction that most quickly gets it back within the fence (the green line)
- the right image shows how the vehicle turns back towards waypoint 1 once it has moved back inside the fence

By the way, this issue could be recreated in SITL by doing the following:

- start SITL rover
- enable BendyRuler by setting OA_TYPE = 1
- enable the Polygon fence by setting FENCE_ENABLE = 1, FENCE_TYPE = 6, FENCE_ACTION = 0 (we don't want it switching to Hold mode) and then create a polygon fence with the mavproxy gui
- temporarily disable the fence by setting FENCE_ENABLE = 0
- arm the vehicle in MANUAL mode and drive outside the fence
- re-enable the fence by setting FENCE_ENABLE 1
- RTL, the vehicle would start home but would then weave as it approached the polygon fence and never cross back within the fence.

The same issue does not exist for the circular fence nor when using Dijksta's.

title: Copter: esc cal startup check moved outside rc output initialisation
body:
This PR resolves this issue:https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/11816 in which the EKF was being upset each time the motor test was run.

The cause of the problem was the main loop was being slowed down during the motor test because we call rc_init_out() when starting the test.  This function includes a call to the esc_calibration_startup_check() function which [includes some delays to ensure we've received radio packets from the user](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/ArduCopter/esc_calibration.cpp#L30).

We definitely **do not** want to be running the esc calibration check when we're running the motors test because it could falsely trigger entry to the esc calibration if the user happens to have the transmitter's throttle stick held high so I've moved esc_calibration_startup_check to only run as part of the vehicle startup initialisation (aka "init_ardupilot").  Note this change also affects compassmot but we don't want to run the esc-calibration-startup-check before compassmot either.

I've re-tested the motor test and the esc calibration on my IRIS and they work fine.  The EKF reporting to the GCS shows the EKF is happy now when the motor test is run

title: Copter: land mode initialises yaw
body:
This resolves an issue with the vehicle's heading changing as it is switched into Land mode because the AutoYaw's mode is not being set as Land mode starts.

Note that this change only affect the Land flight mode.  It does not affect Land-within-Auto or Land-within-RTL.

The sudden change in yaw is most easily reproduced when switching from ZigZag mode to Land mode.  Steps to reproduce in SITL are:

- param set RC8_OPTION 61  (allows setting the zigzag "waypoints")
- take off in Loiter and climb to 5m
- rc8 2000 (to set first zigzag point)
- rc 1 1000 (to fly left 10m)
- rc 1 1500 (to stop)
- rc 8 1000 (to save second zigzag point
- rc 8 2000 (to fly to the first waypoint)
- rc 8 1000 (to fly to the 2nd waypoint)
- LAND (at this point the vehicle will yaw normally to the west)

Below are screen shots of the SITL test (as described above).  Note the desired yaw before and after this PR's change:

title: Fixed I2C errors on high bus noise
body:
This fixes issue #12862 where a cross-connected I2C and UART pin caused a watchdog by causing DMA operations to happen outside an I2C transaction context.
We previously put in a generic interrupt storm mitigation system for the last set of I2C errors, and that did work correctly, but this is a new issue where an interrupt happening outside of an I2C transaction context could trigger the re-enable of a stale DMA operation, causing a memory overwrite
The fix is a "belt and braces" approach where we guarantee we can't get any DMA operations on I2C happening outside a transaction context

title: AP_Rangefinder: use offset param value in all drivers
body:
This PR changes all rangefinder drivers to add the RNGFNDx_OFFSET param value to distances.  This parameter's default is 0 so hopefully it will have no effect for most users.

The change to the PWM driver fixes issue https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/13252 which is a regression in Copter-4.0.0 vs Copter-3.6.12.

For consistency the offset is always added at the moment the distance from the sensor is stored in the _state.distance_cm variable.  I hope this consistency will reduce the possibility of bugs being introduced in the future.

Some things to note:

- the offset is applied before the RNGFND_MIN_CM and RNGFND_MAX_CM values are used to determine the state of the rangefinder.  I think this is correct because this is consistent with how the analog driver and [Copter-3.6.x PWM driver](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/Copter-3.6/libraries/AP_RangeFinder/AP_RangeFinder_PX4_PWM.cpp#L120) used it.
- the AP_RangeFinder_MAVLink driver is inconsistent with other drivers in that it [sets the distance to zero if there is NoData](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/blob/master/libraries/AP_RangeFinder/AP_RangeFinder_MAVLink.cpp#L71).  I have left it reporting "0" as opposed to "0+OFFSET".

@WickedShell,

I see your point but it's got a couple of practical issues that come with it.

1. The OFFSET parameter description pretty clearly says that it is a cm offset for all non-analog drivers.  Clearly it's not and we could of course change the parameter description but this was the intention of the parameter.
2. Only the EKF uses the POS_X/Y/Z parameters and the EKF's height-above-terrain estimate is only used with optical flow (as far as I know).  Most Copter users who have a lidar attached want to do terrain following which, in Copter at least, is done outside the EKF.  This leads us to two possible bits which are large scope creep

   - Switch copter over to using EKF's height-above-terrain estimate
   - Make a new height-above-terrain estimator or enhance Copter's existing estimator to use the POS params

> Only the EKF uses the POS_X/Y/Z parameters and the EKF's height-above-terrain estimate is only used with optical flow (as far as I know).

The EKF may be the only one using it now, but it's definitely not the only one that should be using it. You actually generally speaking want to do attitude correction, particularly on larger vehicles, which needs a full 3D correction.

Basically I'm objecting to this as it's making this harder to handle correctly in the future, unless someone knows to set the POS parameters to 0. title: AP_HAL_ChibiOS:  Fix waf --default-parameters
body:
If a defaults.parm file was present in the hwdef, waf configure ignored the `--default-parameters` command line argument.  It also treated any specified file as it's root being the repo directory, which is not very useful. It would turn an absolute path into something ridiculous like `/home/matt/github/ardupilot/home/matt/Desktop/paramfile.params` which is clearly invalid.

This PR does a few things to fix all this.
- Allow you to specify and absolute path to a parameter file that works, looking like this: `./waf configure CubeOrange --default-parameters=/home/matt/Desktop/paramfile.params`.
- A parameter file specified with the `--default-parameters` argument will take precedent over a `defaults.parm` file in the hwdef directory.
- Additional prints to tell the user what it actually is doing with what files.

It should be noted, which I didn't know until this, that this command line argument is only used in configure.  Not in the build command.

This PR resolves [this user issue raised in the Copter-4.0 category on discuss](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/gimbal-limits-with-storm32-backend-mavlink-not-applied-correctly/51438).

The report was that the camera gimbal was not able to move all the way to the min/max configured angles.  The user had specified the min and max tilt angles as -90 and +10 deg respectively but the gimbal was only moving between -90 and -40 degrees. This PR also makes some formatting changes but happy to remove these if there are any objections.

Just FYI, this change in behaviour comes from this PR:https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/9953 which introduced a reliance on the RCx_TRIM values when calculating the pilot desired target angle.

title: Copter: fix use of WP_NAVALT_MIN
body:
This PR resolves issue https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/12888 which can lead to the vehicle drifting away if the wind is too strong and WP_NAVALT_MIN is set too high.

The underlying cause of the issue is:

- that the current method does not use the WPNav's get_roll() and get_pitch outputs until the vehicle passes the WP_NAVALT_MIN altitude meaning the vehicle could drift horizontally a significant distance
- WPNav will stop advancing the intermediate point if the vehicle is more than the leash length from the track

These two put together mean the vehicle is not trying to move back towards the track nor is it trying to climb to the WP_NAVALT_MIN and it drifts away.

This PR resolves the problem by constantly shifting the track horizontally so that it is where the vehicle is horizontally.  Then at the last iteration just before horizontal control is enabled we move the track to be at the vehicle's "stopping point".

It might seem that we should always just reset the track to the vehicle's stopping point but if the wind was extremely high, the vehicle could end up flying horizontally quite quickly, so quickly that it's stopping point might be longer than the leash and we would be back in the position where the WPNav controller would not advance the intermediate point.

This has been tested in SITL and below are some screen shots.

Below is a picture of the vehicle's track at the moment it starts towards the first waypoint.  The wind was set to 3m/s north so the vehicle has drifted about 30m north before horizontal navigation began.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/75599695-ab3d7480-5aea-11ea-9478-c1d8d1a11349.png)

Here's a before image of the PSC.TPX (target North-South position) vs PX (actual North-South position) showing the vehicle drifts 200m before it passes the WP_NAVALT_MIN altitude and retakes horizontal control (i.e. the altitude climbed very slowly)
![before-image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/75599905-96fa7700-5aec-11ea-842e-f2a20332c4f2.png)

Here's an after image showing the vehicle drifts only 28m horizontally before re-taking horizontal control at the moment it passes the WP_NAVALT_MIN altitude.
![after-image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/75599951-1daf5400-5aed-11ea-948c-e3ab8db74c3d.png)

Here's an after image of the roll, pitch and altitude.  We see the roll and pitch angles are relatively smooth (i.e. no sudden twitches).  Throttle output (not shown) is also smooth during the transition
![after-roll-pitch](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/75600036-0e7cd600-5aee-11ea-958b-ad6ed93ee442.png)

title: Hold CS pins high in bootloader - fixes param reset issue
body:
This fixes the param reset issue related to #13621 and #13581 
The issue with param reset was finally tracked down to not holding the FRAM CS pin high in the bootloader. Electrical noise on the SPI bus while in the bootloader could cause the FRAM to become corrupt if the CS pin is floating. This has been confirmed by one user (Luke Wylie) who was able to reproduce the issue reliably. With the bootloader updated with this fix the issue can no longer be reproduced.
Many thanks to Luke for doing so much testing of this issue for us!

body:
This fixes a problem in TradHeli with the Alt Hold angle limiter being active at hover collective pitch. The max throttle definition in the parent class only applies to multi-rotor aircraft that need more overhead for attitude control. title: Copter/Rover/Plane/Tracker: fix velocity sent in GLOBAL_POSITION_INT message
body:
This PR fixes two things to do with the sending of the GLOBAL_POSITION_INT message to the ground stations and companion computers:

- for all vehicles, fix velocity z-axis field in GLOBAL_POSITION_INT to be in NED format (i.e. +ve is down) to be consistent with the mavlink protocol (http://mavlink.org/messages/common#GLOBAL_POSITION_INT).
- for sub, rover and copter, use the system time instead of the last GPS fix time.  This is correct because our position comes from the EKF not the GPS.  We also get the velocity directly from the AHRS object instead of the inertial-nav library (which we plan to remove and is just a shim on the underlying EKFs)

The only known downside to these changes is the velocity for Rover, Sub and Copter will not appear in the GLOBAL_POSITION_INT message until the EKF has initialised.  It is possible we could fall back to the GPS velocities in case the EKF does not have a good velocity estimate but I don't think this is necessary.  The GPS position and velocities are already available through the GPS_RAW_INT message (albeit using ground course and ground speed instead of a 3D vector)

title: Rover: fix forward-back acceleration limiting
body:
This PR fixes [this issue](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/8426) found in [this discussion](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/skid-steer-mower-overshooting-pivot-turns/28910).

The issue was that when first engaging the speed controller, we were not acceleration limiting the desired-speed, instead we simply let the desired-speed jump up to whatever the caller requested.  With this change, in these situations we limited the desired-speed using the vehicle's current speed as a base.

To test this change was correct, a SITL rover was loaded with a very simple mission (just one waypoint) and then soon after arming, the vehicle was switched from MANUAL mode to AUTO.  Below is a graph of the desired speed vs actual speed and we can see in the "BEFORE" image that the desired speed immediately spikes up to the WP_SPEED (set to 5m/s) while in the "AFTER" image it rises more slowly.

![before-after](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/40216653-008bc710-5aa3-11e8-927c-67cebb83c0cd.png)

title: Rover: allow steering to Motors beyond -1 to +1 range
body:
This PR attempts to resolve and issue with loss of steering control for vehicles traveling at high speeds.  This issue was caused by [this earlier PR](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/8312) which moved the speed-scaling from the attitude controller to the motors library.  The potential issue was recognised and sadly now it's been confirmed during beta testing.  Comments from the PR are copied below:

> the potential downside of the change is that at very high speeds the steering control may become so limited that it cannot counteract a physical misalignment in the steering linkage. For example at 20m/s (70km/h) only 5% of the total steering range is available. **A potential solution to this though is to allow steering inputs > 1.**
> 

This PR resolved the problem by allowing the high-level steering request sent to the motors to be outside the -1 to +1 range.

Below are images before and after showing the simulated vehicle is better able to achieve the desired turn rate.  In this test an Ackermann style rover (i.e. separate throttle and steering controls) was driven slowly (2m/s) but with full left steering.  In master, because the speed scaling, the steering output was scaled back too far to achieve the desired turn rate.  With this PR the vehicle comes much closer.

![master-turnrate](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/41139637-d9aad618-6b23-11e8-8060-58aa65a00b7f.png)
![new-turnrate](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/41139638-db769d74-6b23-11e8-9d96-7be20f00a8f0.png)

Somewhat separately this PR also adds a new parameter MOT_SPD_SCA_BASE (i.e. "Motor Speed Scaling Base") which is equivalent to the similar "Vector Thrust Scaling Base" parameter.  It allows the user to specify the lowest speed that the scaling is applied.  I don't expect many people to change this but it could be useful especially for very slow vehicles because it will give them better steering control below 1m/s.  Very fast vehicles that spend very little time below 1m/s.

title: EKF: Fix bad roundoff and inconsistent altitude handling
body:
This addresses the #9420 reported by @horiuchi4dn. The core problem this is trying to address is accidentally forcing the getLLH method of the EKF to always be rounded to 1 meter. This was less serious then it sounded as any call through `AP_AHRS::get_position` full reset the altitude anyways, but it can propegate into `AP_AHRS::get_location()`.

This corrects this by moving the logic that `AP_AHRS_NavEKF` was applying to live inside of the getLLH method and doesn't require get_position to do the reset. This has 2 side effects:
- `getLLH` could return true before even if we didn't have a valid vertical position (`get_position` couldn't so this should be minimal impact, and those places I can see that are affected actually benefit from the protection). 
- `getLLH` was not correctly applying the `posOffsetNED.z` correction which means that `getLLH` was returning incorrect results if you had an offset accelerometer. Again it's a small change that I believe is correct and won't affect most locations.

Final note: I'd like to remove `AP_AHRS::get_location()` but I will probably leave that for a separate PR.

EDIT: Worth noting that this should improve reported position error in replay as replay was using getLLH to compare the error.

title: AP_RangeFinder: Benewake sends max-range+1m when out of range
body:
This PR corrects two issues discovered during Copter-3.6.1-rc1 testing ([see discussion here](https://discuss.ardupilot.org/t/copter-3-6-1-rc1-is-available-for-beta-testing/34787/9)):

- The Benewake lidar driver returns the RNGFND_MAX_CM + 1m if the lidar goes out of range.  Previously it would ignore these readings but this would lead to the lidar's state becoming "NoData" when really it's "OutOfRangeHigh".  The 1m addition to the defined maximum range is a bit arbitrary but I wanted to ensure that it's significantly beyond the maximum so that no rounding errors could lead to it being considered within range.  Below is a screen shot of a test where the RNGFND_MAX_CM was set to 1500 so the lidar reports 16m when out-of-range.

![benewake-test](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1498098/48174157-22755500-e34a-11e8-981e-0b0b42082fce.png)


- Copter's extended system status message to the GCS reports the lidar as healthy as long as it's returning data.  Previously the lidar was only reported healthy if the lidar range was within the MIN and MAX.  In my view, "healthy" means the lidar is operating as expected and no action is required from the user.  It's a normal and expected thing in most situations that the lidar will go out of range of the ground so I don't think it's good to report the lidar as "unhealthy" in these situations.
symptom: Benewake sends max-range+1m when out of range

title: Battery current for MAVLink is not scaled correctly
body:
@LorenzMeier 
Apart from hardware issues discussed [here](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/px4users/bI1-ZbecoN8), there is also software bug. Yesterday we noticed that we don't get a current reading via MAVLink but it is logged correctly. To be more precise, the current reading we got over MAVLink was 0 or 1.

In https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/0e26c2b37b362c19d30f0544ed6d21bc408bcd7d/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_messages.cpp#L550 and https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/0e26c2b37b362c19d30f0544ed6d21bc408bcd7d/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_messages.cpp#L575 the battery current for MAVLink get's divided by 10. The target field is uint16. According to specs it's supposed to contain milliamps \* 10. This suggests that the source field contains milliamps, but as far as I can tell it actually contains amps. This would match the effect we saw for currents between 0 and 15 amps.

The scaling for the MAVLink message changed during the last commit.

title: Passthrough mode for Snapdragon on PixFalcon fails to output PWM
body:
I am using a PixFalcon in passthrough mode to control the ESCs with the Snapdragon flight.
The PixFalcon refuses to talk to the ESCs, which beep every few seconds as a result.

I am seeing this on the current master (af02b860b3cc495f67a879088dca9f8b1edd58f9) with the following procedure:
Flash the firmware to the PixFalcon
`make px4fmu-v2_default upload`
With the SD card out, connect to the NuttShell. Set a normal airframe and reboot:

```
param set SYS_AUTOSTART 10020
reboot
```

Once rebooted, re-connect, press the safety switch and test the PWM:

```
pwm test -c 1 -p 1200
```

The motor turns, the ESCs are quiet.
Set the passthrough airframe and reboot (via the nsh command, **not** power-cycling):

```
param set SYS_AUTOSTART 20000
reboot
```

Re-connect and test the PWM (safety switch not required)

```
pwm test -c 1 -p 1200
```

The motor turns, the ESCs are quiet. If I `reboot`, the PixFalcon's LED will now light up purple instead of blinking blue, but `pwm test` still works.

As soon as I power-cycle, `pwm test` no longer works (and neither does `snapdragon_rc_pwm`).
After stopping `pwm test` with `Ctrl-C` I get the following message:

```
pwm: PWM_SERVO_SET(0): Invalid argument
```

I see the same output printed in [`snapdragon_rc_pwm`](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/2f48317a9ea7b05d8c61b3d1c44f8229491350b1/src/drivers/snapdragon_rc_pwm/snapdragon_rc_pwm.cpp#L209), where `ret == -1` and `errno == 22`.

title: Snapdragon: some parameters don't want to stick
body:
The param `PWM_DISARMED` just doesn't seem to stick/get saved on Snapdragon.

Also reported by @blandry.
comments:
[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2016-04-25T13:01:31Z | updated=2016-04-25T13:01:31Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214305639
The param seems to appear and work after `param set PWM_DISARMED 900` has been called once.

@LorenzMeier any idea why this is necessary?


---

[issue_comment] LorenzMeier | created=2016-04-25T13:03:43Z | updated=2016-04-25T13:03:43Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214307171
So you're saying that accessing it via MAVLink doesn't work, but on the shell does? Which shell? qshell or Linux side?


---

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2016-04-25T13:07:34Z | updated=2016-04-25T13:07:34Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214309779
With `param set PWM_DISARMED 900` I mean the Linux side.

When QGC/mavlink is used, it is also `set` on the Linux side, however, the `save` happens on the QURT side. During the save, the written param is not in the list here:
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/systemlib/param/param_shmem.c#L986


---

[issue_comment] LorenzMeier | created=2016-04-25T13:12:01Z | updated=2016-04-25T13:12:01Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214312786
I'm pretty sure that the list logic there is wrong i.e. its dirty bit is not set or evaluated correctly. Note that there is a "unsaved", "non-default" and "used flag" and those have to be used correctly.


---

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2016-04-25T13:15:35Z | updated=2016-04-25T13:25:09Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214315886
The "used flag" is not used on Snapdragon.

~~I just checked, and you can set a param from default to something in QGC/mavlink and it won't get saved with either: `param save` or `qshell param save`.~~

You can set a param from default to something in QGC/mavlink and it won't stick if you do `qshell param save` but it works with `param save`.


---

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2016-04-25T13:26:07Z | updated=2016-04-25T13:26:07Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214326269
The problem seems **not** to be the "unsaved" flag here:
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/systemlib/param/param_shmem.c#L980


---

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2016-04-25T19:26:20Z | updated=2016-04-25T19:26:20Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214491268
@mcharleb this is the param sync issue that I was telling you about earlier.


---

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2016-04-26T07:15:58Z | updated=2016-04-26T07:15:58Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214647428
The problem is essentially that the local list of changed parameters on the DSP side is not kept up to date with what is changed from looking at the shared memory.

The local list not in sync is `param_values` in https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/systemlib/param/param_shmem.c#L971.

If you do `qshell show param PWM_DISARMED` it will update the local list and realize that it has been changed.

@LorenzMeier any advice how to patch this?


---

[issue_comment] LorenzMeier | created=2016-04-26T07:19:09Z | updated=2016-04-26T07:19:09Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214649544
We need a param update / check API on the DSP side and then register it with the existing always-running daemons (e.g. the HRT) to run regularly.


---

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2016-04-26T07:22:06Z | updated=2016-04-26T07:22:06Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214650606
But that would cause a race with the param save because you want to do the update before you do a save.


---

[issue_comment] LorenzMeier | created=2016-04-26T07:23:31Z | updated=2016-04-26T07:23:31Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214651200
The right way to do this is to establish a lock so they can't race and of course always run the param update before a save.

It actually sounds like this is all what you need to do for now, since the param changed publication makes it to the DSP and we don't need a background process?


---

[issue_comment] julianoes | created=2016-04-26T07:27:21Z | updated=2016-04-26T07:27:21Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/4356#issuecomment-214652811
Ok, right. So I guess, the param update needs to loop through all params and check whether they have been changed. I'm trying to find the param from looking at the changed bit, that would be less cycles.

5) the drone will return home (RTL_STATE_RETURN)
6) the drone will start descending (RTL_STATE_DESCEND)
7) pause the drone
8) fly to another location
9) start RTL again

its much more critical if during RTL mode its goes as far to RTL_STATE_LAND mode.

title: Takeoff overshoot in real world but not in the simulator
body:
When I ask the drone to take off to 5 meters it shoots aggressively up to 10 meters then comes back down:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/18707114/24180121/4e9fbc48-0e70-11e7-8c1c-51aff459651c.png)

[14-25-29-input.zip](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/files/860207/14-25-29-input.zip)

Looking at the code in mc_pos_control, around line 1561 under the comment "special thrust setpoint generation for takeoff from ground" I see that it ramps up throttle all the way to MPC_THR_MAX if necessary in order to get the drone off the ground, and when it detects drone has reached MPC_TKO_SPEED speed then it switches to normal setpoint altitude hold.  The problem I see with this is that the GPS sensor is very slow, so it always cranks to MPC_THR_MAX for very agressive takeoff.  

I want to fix this, but I could use some pointers.  I don't want any new parameters, we already have too many, instead I would love the code to be self tuning, for example, if I strap something heavy on my drone, it should "just work".  I assume that the current behavior came about because you also do not want the drone to "hop" during takeoff because then it thinks it has landed again and disarms.  

But clearly from the picture above, PWM shot all the way to up max throttle (90% of 1950 is 1755) before it even detected drone leaving the ground, then because the acceleration was so great, even with PWM falling quickly to 1283, the drone was essentially flung up to 10 meters.    What is very interesting is the red line I drew on the PWM signal.  Drone is still ascending quickly, and PWM is going up??? from 1283 to 1443.  I realize you don't want the drone to freefall, but there must be something wrong there.

So I propose to add a takeoff that is more gentle, like landing.  Where it slowly spins up the props just to get some idea of what it takes to get any vertical acceleration.  For example, when I look at the charts, z-mag responded 1 full second before GPS noticed any change.  In fact, z-mag was seeing something when PWM was way down at 1100.  This slow ramp up ensures safety, if anyone is near they will back off before it shoots up into the air.  So from there it should ramp up quickly to HOVER_THROTTLE + some delta, where that delta is self tuning.  This sudden ramp will cause a hop, but to keep it in the air we need more than hover throttle, so it can start more aggressively to ensure no hops, but then it will write a private setting to calibrate this value so that the next take off will be smoother and smoother each time you try it.  This is a little bit like auto-tuning a PID algorithm I suppose.

Any objections or better ideas ?

I think the problem with takeoff overshoot comes from the hover throttle feedforward added in 5529023 that is not taken into account in the takeoff code:
```C++
// copter has reached our takeoff speed. split the thrust setpoint up
// into an integral part and into a P part
_thrust_int(2) = _takeoff_thrust_sp - _params.vel_p(2) * fabsf(_vel(2));
```

Try something like this instead:
```C++
_thrust_int(2) = _takeoff_thrust_sp - _params.vel_p(2) * fabsf(_vel(2)) - _params.thr_hover;
```

If you reduce the P and I velocity gains from the default in the simulator you can probably see the overshoot there as well.

title: Possible Bug in HIL_STATE_QUATERNION handling
body:
Hi,
@TSC21 and I are developing HIL plugins in MAVROS. This is to allow any ROS-compatible simulator to be used in HIL setup.

In the decoding of HIL_STATE_QUATERNION msg, in PX4 firmware, specifically the ```vehicle_global_position```,
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/ecb2511a7bbad094bff23dd95036eda0656778f0/src/modules/simulator/simulator_mavlink.cpp#L402-L413
altitude is divided by ```1E3```, but ```lat/lon``` are not scaled down properly. In the msg definition,
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/912ed98a28022504ef3ec4bf1bce0fe041f83ac4/msg/vehicle_global_position.msg

```lat/lon/alt``` are assumed to be in deg/deg/meters. And, they are supposed to be received in deg 1E7 and meters 1E3 according to 
https://pixhawk.ethz.ch/mavlink/#HIL_STATE_QUATERNION

So, I guess that 
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/ecb2511a7bbad094bff23dd95036eda0656778f0/src/modules/simulator/simulator_mavlink.cpp#L407-L408
should be divided by 1E7.

Also the ```vehicle_global_position``` msg does not have ```timestamp``` field,

So, possibly another mistake here,
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/ecb2511a7bbad094bff23dd95036eda0656778f0/src/modules/simulator/simulator_mavlink.cpp#L404

Thanks.

title: Yaw/thrust saturation and loss of control during flight
body:
Hi everyone,

During a position control flight with my VTOL (in MC mode only), I encountered a really strange behavior. After flying perfectly well, the yaw control was suddenly lost and the drone was loosing altitude.

![esc_response2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/14822839/26549616/2bc1ae62-447a-11e7-81eb-4d79c5c93205.png)

As you can see, around t=59s, the drone did not respond to the yaw command even if the ESC reported acceleration and deceleration of the motors. After that between t=63s and t=69s, the drone is spinning around it's yaw axis and since it was loosing altitude, the thrust did reach saturation, without any RPM response.

I'm suspecting a mixer saturation or an ESC issue. 

Link to the complete [log](http://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=55960095-7efd-4e28-8acc-1854828e75bc).

Finally, my setup is a PixHawk Pro with Orel 20 ESCs and a mRo GPS.

I maybe found the issue in the `mixer_multirotor.cpp` file ([link](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/systemlib/mixer/mixer_multirotor.cpp#L326-L337)).
```
} else if (out > 1.0f) {
			// allow to reduce thrust to get some yaw response
			float prop_reduction = fminf(0.15f, out - 1.0f);
			// keep the maximum requested reduction
			thrust_reduction = fmaxf(thrust_reduction, prop_reduction);

			if (fabsf(_rotors[i].yaw_scale) <= FLT_EPSILON) {
				yaw = 0.0f;

			} else {
				yaw = (1.0f - ((roll * _rotors[i].roll_scale + pitch * _rotors[i].pitch_scale) *
					       roll_pitch_scale + thrust + boost)) / _rotors[i].yaw_scale;
}
```
When the output saturates, the `thrust_reduction` is computed but the new yaw value is then computed again with the old unreduced thrust. The final result is then a reduced thrust with no yaw control.

@LorenzMeier I am in favor of turning off the landdetector alt max for now, since in order to implement it properly it requires some more changes. Currently the landdetector adjusts max altitude based on battery level. Lets assume the vehicle is flying a mission. It is possible to adjust the desired altitude to the max altitude, but what happens if the vehicle is in between two waypoints and the battery level goes below the threshold which results in a lower max altitude. The navigator  already has set the current waypoint and does not know about the altitude max change and will therefore set a mission altitude above the max.
In order to solve that, the navigator also needs to know when the max altitude has changed and then update the mission item accordingly. However, before I implement something like that I prefer to clean up the navigator first such that waypoints are actually only sent when they have changed.

here is a branch where I moved the altitude limit to the navigator and removed the altitude limit from the position controller and land-detector.
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/tree/pr-limit_altitude_navigator

the reason why I did that:
- a detector should just detect an event, but should not apply any action as it was done in the land-detector for altitude limitation
- the battery level is already handled/detected by the battery.cpp class. Hence, it is not necessary to do another detection in the land-detector

title: FW Land mode = crash
body:
I recently had a flight that put up a "[commander] failsafe: no global position warning", then switched to Land mode and proceeded to fly straight into the earth. My main concern is why the global position was lost in the first place (did the estimated position and gps position begin to differ too much? why?), but it would be nice to know that there is a reliable FW solution for this sort of condition to return to the ground hopefully in one piece.

Log here: http://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=b7fcb8a9-a66f-4b49-94e3-f896d3a65cb7
comments:
[issue_comment] JonReacher | created=2017-07-13T04:05:13Z | updated=2017-07-13T04:05:13Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-314964724
I know there are several ways that you could go about returning to the ground as safely as possible. In this particular case it seems that if the autopilot would have trusted the gps and disregarded position estimation everything would have been fine. If it truly is flying blind, or thinks it is, and no dead reckoning is available, would it be best to go into a descending loiter at a slow target speed, say FW_LND_AIRSPD_SC?

---

[issue_comment] dagar | created=2017-07-13T04:39:53Z | updated=2017-07-13T04:39:53Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-314968755
There's an open loop loiter GPS failure mode, but I'd rather use the FW position controller to execute a heading hold landing while controlling airspeed. The main blocker to this at the moment is the FW position controller (TECS + L1) runs based on global position updates. I'm thinking of how to refactor it to continue running TECS.

---

[issue_comment] Antiheavy | created=2017-07-18T16:08:09Z | updated=2017-07-18T16:08:09Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-316113824
A more typical loss of GPS failsafe in the world of fixed wing UAVs is to spiral down so as to hit the ground as close to the last reported GPS location as possible.  If you just heading hold you will likely get blown far downwind before hitting the ground - from 400 feet altitude a typical fixed wing might glide for over a mile downwind.

I'd vote for something like this:

1) Loss of GPS failsafe timeout ( 0.5 to 10 seconds depending on how long the given system can be expected to safely operate without GPS and/or without global position from the EKF).
2) Failsafe trigger
3) Set throttle = 0
4) Spiral down slowly holding airspeed: set to cruise speed or maybe minimum speed, hold a fixed bank angle
5) if GPS regained switch to Hold mode

If you were in a mission when you lost GPS and then it came back shouldn't the mission resume?

[issue_comment] Antiheavy | created=2017-07-18T20:57:19Z | updated=2017-07-18T20:57:19Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-316195419
> If you were in a mission when you lost GPS and then it came back shouldn't the mission resume?

hmmm...  yeah, maybe you are right.   I'm thinking about if the vehicle descends down low and then decides to turn and start resuming the mission in some bad direction right into some trees or something, then again I don't know that Hold mode would be any better.   Less confusing to just resume whatever it was doing previously I suppose.  

---

[issue_comment] JonReacher | created=2017-07-19T22:20:38Z | updated=2017-07-19T22:21:25Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-316535841
I very much agree with spiraling down. Linear landing is scary for many reasons. A plane in a linear descent with a shallow glide angle can cover some serious ground before hitting who knows what.  At least with a descending loiter you have a reasonable expectation of the general "terrain" it will land in. The alternative may travel away from a safe flying area to the next town. I fly on a ridge with a small city visible in the distance below a few miles away. One failsafe could set it on a course for real trouble.
  Is it too simple to just use the GPS failsafe navigation settings for the global position loss, except maybe with a scaled down throttle setting to ensure slow descent?  These should already be set for a holding loiter, at a reasonable radius for the specific aircraft.
  I'm no coder, but could you point to those parameters in case of a failsafe, then add a percent scale down, for example?

---

[issue_comment] priseborough | created=2017-07-31T03:15:41Z | updated=2017-07-31T03:15:41Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-318957529
The current practice of fixed wing failsafe going into an open loop control mode is dangerous and often results in a high speed spiral dive, endangering people on the ground and providing little time for recovery. 

For fixed wing vehicles I would like to see addition of a CIRCLE_DESCENT mode that enables the plane to be put into a zero throttle, constant bank, constant pitch condition to provide a controlled slow speed spiral descent. If we assume that only the attitude solution is valid, then we cannot use TECS, so controlling to a specified pitch angle will be required. 

The only time the open loop mode should be used as the failsafe for fixed wing is when the attitude data in the control state message is invalid.

> If we assume that only the attitude solution is valid, then we cannot use TECS, so controlling to a specified pitch angle will be required.

2 cents: if valid airspeed (and baro altitude for that matter) are present they should be used instead of constant pitch.



> fixed wing failsafe going into an open loop control mode is dangerous and often results in a high speed spiral dive, endangering people on the ground

here is a recent fixed wing flight log where this exact spiral dive happened resulting in destruction of the vehicle:

The existing speed and height control loops (TECS) requires derivative states that are not available from using Baro or GPS directly, so until TECS algorithms are modified to generate this data internally, attitude control will have to do and will be a lot better than what we have currently.

[issue_comment] priseborough | created=2017-07-31T05:17:39Z | updated=2017-07-31T05:17:39Z | https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/7609#issuecomment-318970098
I've been working on a progressive series of improvements to make the ekf faster to recover from a loss of navigation caused by bad magnetometer data. https://github.com/PX4/ecl/pull/294 a resulted in significant improvement in the ability to handle bad compass data and https://github.com/PX4/ecl/pull/313 will result in further improvements in that area when it has been tuned and tested.

The major remaining challenge is how to handle bad inertial data caused by excessive vibration levels. This can strike without warning in flight when RPM changes and structural resonances are excited and can make inertial navigation impossible.  What we need in that instance is a fallback mode that make minimal use of the accelerometer data. Until we disable the DLPF in the IMU and perform all digital processing in the driver, we will not be able to reliably detect clipping in the inertial sensors.

title: vmount causes system freeze
body:
I'm trying to use `vmount` with mavlink inputs (`MNT_MODE_IN 3`, i.e. `MAVLINK_DO_MOUNT`) and with mavlink output (`MNT_MODE_OUT 1`, i.e. `MAV_CMD_DO_MOUNT_CONTROL`).

### Steps to reproduce
- Flash current master
- reset all parameters
- on the console:
```
param set MNT_MODE_IN 3
param set MNT_MODE_OUT 1
vmount start
```


I suspect the problem lies in the fact that in this configuration, the `vmount` input `InputMavlinkCmdMount` subscribes to `vehicle_command` and the output `OutputMavlink` publishes on it, causing a loop.

I tried preventing `InputMavlinkCmdMount` from processing messages that were published by `OutputMavlink` by checking [here](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/925efe990d0b17e2c976f51e56860e38b9cc2ba6/src/drivers/vmount/input_mavlink.cpp#L229) that the system and component IDs don't match the one's that `vmount` itself is publishing, but it didn't help.

title: Mixer of Bormatec Maja not working in Manual Override
body:
While testing the v1.6.5 of the PX4 I found the following issue:

During normal flight operation everything works as expected. In case of an FMU crash in the manual flight mode the OVERRIDE flag is correctly set in the px4io. However, in this mode the outputs for MAIN 1, MAIN 3 through MAIN 5 are correctly set. But the MAIN 2 (right aileron) output remains always at 1500 which corresponds to a zero deflection.

This behavior can be solved by removing the lines for the airbrakes ([L24](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/ROMFS/px4fmu_common/mixers/AAERTWF.main.mix#L24), [L29](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/ROMFS/px4fmu_common/mixers/AAERTWF.main.mix#L29)), or changing the index from 6 to a value lower than 4. However, I was not able to identify why an index value of 6 or higher breaks the mixing.

See also this topic in the [forum](http://discuss.px4.io/t/failsafe-in-case-of-an-fmu-crash-for-an-airplane/4209/5).

* Flow Firmware: QGC provided firmware (PX4/Flow/master)

When the flow data goes invalid, the EKF continues to dead-reckon and neither the vehicle_local_position_0.vxy_reset_counter or vehicle_local_position_0.xy_reset_counter increments during the log indicating that the apparent state reset and subsequent filter instability was caused by fusing the flow data without first resetting the position and velocity states and their corresponding covariances.

title: [Multicopter mixer] Wrongly computed mixing tables
body:
I was checking the new [mixer generator](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/lib/mixer/geometries/tools/px_generate_mixers.py) script from @jlecoeur  in order to add my specific multicopter geometry and I found that it produces values that didn't match my mixing table generated by a custom script.
After checking the generator, I found that the table generated doesn't match the mixing strategy used in PX4.
The table generated has the following coefficients for each actuator:
```
roll_gain | pitch_gain | yaw_gain | thrust_gain
``` 
And has to be used like this: 
`out = roll_gain*roll + pitch_gain*pitch + yaw_gain*yaw + thrust_gain*thrust` (which is the standard matrix*vector multiplication)
However, in PX4, the equation is 
`out = (roll_gain*roll + pitch_gain*pitch + yaw_gain*yaw + thrust)*out_gain` 
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/26d95ef67479b90212f5ea8255d43721865ff904/src/lib/mixer/mixer_multirotor.cpp#L188-L192

At the current state, there is a confusion and the `thrust_gain` generated in the tables is used as the `out_gain` which lead to an incorrect mixing and produces unexpected coupling between the axes.

This can be corrected in two different ways:
1. Fix the generator script to match firmware implementation
2. Change the PX4 implementation to use a simple matrix-style mixer

Since the gain of each motor can be chosen in the geometry config file, and that the matrix-style mixing table is simpler and more intuitive, I would prefer to use the 2nd alternative.
FYI @MaEtUgR @jlecoeur

title: Incorrect handling of baud rate values in RTPS
body:
**Bug Report**

This is a problem with the fast RTPS code. 

For both client and agent code, baud rate values are generated from the program argument by converting the argument directly to a number. However in termios.h, the baud rate is encoded in a number of preset values, eg B57600. This affects the agent running on Ubuntu since the encoded value is different from the actual baud rate. UART transport: device: /dev/ttyUSB1; baudrate: 57600; sleep: 1us; poll: 0ms

UART transport: device: /dev/ttyUSB1; baudrate: 57600; sleep: 1us; poll: 0ms

no flush
sensor_combined publisher started

title: Manual control setpoint pitch is inverted
body:
Pitch is [commonly defined](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7e/Rollpitchyawplain.png) as the righthand rotation around the y axis. Any variable (especially those which are used for inter-app communication) should adhere to this standard.

In the current master branch the field `pitch` of [manual_control_setpoint_s](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/master/src/modules/uORB/topics/manual_control_setpoint.h) is inverted.

It seems that the change was introduced with commit 1d5f62d890d1d85cef5e0f8e282d8e9e70717d46 [starting from here.](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/commit/1d5f62d890d1d85cef5e0f8e282d8e9e70717d46#diff-b2cdb687c37812923ec65dc8fc767506L1400)

Before the commit the pitch value was mapped from the RC value with:

```
/*
* pitch input - stick down is negative, but stick down is pitching up (pos) in NED,
 * so reverse sign.
*/
manual_control.pitch = limit_minus_one_to_one(-1.0f * _rc.chan[_rc.function[PITCH]].scaled);
```

afterwards/now it is mapped with

```
manual_control.pitch = get_rc_value(PITCH, -1.0, 1.0);
```

so the previous correct sign change got lost.

Because the current state is confusing and wrong we have to either _rename_ the name of the variables in manual_control_setpoint_s or we have to _revert the sign change_. I am in favor of reverting the sign change.

I found the following commits related to the above change (directly after 1d5f62d890d1d85cef5e0f8e282d8e9e70717d46 in the commit history): 6f38ed3b4b6f266098d0616b6bd3c18ffe082755 e2ac5222d812bdbfaf33fc2d320ee22ab861d433 ef8b97437342401a464bcc844d6c347c33919d73

rand() returns a integer and x1 and x2 are supposed to be from a uniform random distribution between +- 1.0 so so lines  522 and 523 should be

     x1 = 2.0 * ((double)rand() / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;
     x2 = 2.0 * ((double)rand() / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;

If we had ranf() available to us, that would be a more efficient way of generating x1 and x2.

Use of Gaussian/Normal distributions is common in robotics and flight vehicle simulation, so support for this in the math library would be appropriate.
